title: Lessons from Lionel Dupeaud, Henry Julian's teacher
summary: He last took lessons from Dupeaud, and promises to find his address.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well, there's only one thing I'd like to mention concerning the fellas that I've taken lessons from.
The last fella that I've taken a few lessons from was Lionel Dupal. You ever heard of him?
I don't know him at all. I've heard of him. He don't play anymore,
but he was a good musician.
Is he still here? He's the one
that taught Henry Julian. You ever heard of Henry Julian?

Well, that was Henry Julian's grandfather. He was a saxophone player with the Olympic Band. And when I joined the Olympic Band, well, he got me to go to his grandfather for lessons. Lionel Dupal had not taken lessons, a few lessons with him.
Yeah. He's living. He's a bricklayer, I think. He's a plasterer or a bricklayer.
Do you have his address? We'd like to talk to him sometime, too, you know?
Well, I may be able to get it out the phone book. It's in the phone book. You think it's in the phone book? Yeah, it should be.
D, yeah. If you don't mind, I'll get it for you before you leave.
Yes. How do you spell the last name?
I think it's D-U-P-E-A-U-D. That's why I tell you, he best let me look for you. Yes.
